patients.label: 49-year-old man with HIV-1 infection and a right popliteal mycotic aneurysm with critical limb ischaemia

identity_evidence.quote: the patient was a 49-year-old married male teacher

attribution_limitations: The abstract states the diagnosis by pelvic limb CT angiography, while the results paragraph and Figure 2 caption name angiography of the lower or pelvic limbs; the source does not state they are the same study beyond the Figure 2 citation, so no further merge is made.
The white cell value is printed as "2.9,000/ml"; the number and unit are kept as text and not parsed or reinterpreted.

The discussion sentences on pain with shiny skin at pre-rupture and on hyperkalaemia and systemic microthrombi do not name this patient (only the following sentence about the extrasystoles does), and no potassium value or thrombus imaging is reported in the case, so they are recorded review_only; the claim that ischaemic complications explain the extrasystoles is an author interpretation and is not recorded as a cause.

The clinical tumour is described as 30cm by 23cm, the Figure 3 caption gives a 12cm spongy mass and the operation removed 1,800 g of clots; the source does not state these describe the same measurement, so they are not reconciled.

The patient perspective statement ("I hope to regain the functionality of my limb after surgery") is a patient wish and is not recorded as a plan or outcome; the culture or microbiology performed is not described, only that no germs could be isolated. The discussion also says the mechanisms of bacterial infection could not be established with certainty; no bacterial infection fact is created.

The discussion says 'As in our patient, Dua et al. found apyrexia in 70% of cases, with similar symptoms, associated with a portal of entry located in the lower limb', while the examination reports a slight fever and no spontaneously visible entry point. The scope of 'As in our patient' is unclear, so the examination findings are kept and no apyrexia or portal-of-entry fact is created.

claims.text: A 49-year-old married male teacher, HIV-1 positive for eight years and receiving irregular antiretroviral treatment, presented with a painful swelling of the lower third of the right thigh that had appeared three weeks before admission, with intermittent claudication.
